question.text: Mr. Karan Mehta is studying buy-out variants. He reads that a particular structure 'emerges from the MBO when certain elements are missing from the incumbent management team and therefore have to be sourced from outside'. Which buy-out variant is this?

explanation.text: The Logic: MBI is defined as a variation of MBO in which the management team is assembled from outside because certain elements are missing from the incumbent management team. The 'outside-management-team' cue is the defining characteristic. The Trap: Option A describes a financing structure, not a management-sourcing structure. Option B is the parent concept — MBI is the variant where the team comes from outside. Option D refers to an exit to another buyout fund, not the sourcing of the management team. Note: MBO, MBI and LBO can all coexist in the same deal — they describe distinct dimensions (incumbent team, external team, and financing leverage respectively).
